scope: Opt-in procedural balance, bounded gradual reach, articulated falls and assisted recovery using native Football animations; preserve approved default training and fixed-player match.
platform: Linux rendered software OpenGL with SDL virtual Xbox input; final Windows x64 cross-build packaged separately.
windows_runtime: PE architecture, DLL dependency closure, resource equality, launcher contents, archive integrity and linked-code equality checked. Windows GUI and a physical Xbox controller were not run here.
integration_fixes: Refresh the native mental-image snapshot during physical motion; its 300 ms lifetime cannot span a complete fall.
Separate fixed-step physics integration from source-pose evaluation: every native animation phase sampled within a tick uses the current pose, without advancing dynamics twice.
Preserve authored source preparation and strike poses during queued first-time actions, including headers.
Avoid unnecessary stance IK on unchanged strike poses, which could shorten a fully extended native leg.
Reset queued human actions when switching profiles or returning from a fall; throttle repeated responses to continuous body contact.

research_limits: Scientific sources and one short monocular dead-ball kick were consulted. No exhaustive match-video library, calibrated 3D biomechanics, trained policy or external motion assets were imported.
limitations: Active locomotion remains animation-driven with procedural posture/IK. Free articulated dynamics apply to falls, with assisted get-up.
Ground contacts use approximate segment proxies and root generalized mass/inertia; there is no full coupled articulated solver or general self-collision.
In matches only the controlled actor uses the experimental rig; CPU players retain the approved native movement.
Passive body-ball collision retains the native aerial-ball filter; low rolling balls against a fallen body do not yet have general articulated collision coverage.
The 270 parameter combinations validate numerical variation using three native source poses; they are not 270 new motion-capture clips or exhaustive gameplay coverage.

A pre-existing intermittent Chest_Run reception failure was documented in docs/player-match-validation.json. Its dedicated moving-reception suite was not rerun or claimed repaired by this physical-body change; standing chest and action regressions passed.
Rendered fixtures cover finite input sequences. Visual quality, recovery transitions and physical-controller feel still need evaluation on the Windows gaming PC.
